questions.prompt: What does Stream-K divide equally among blocks?
questions.explanation: Work-centric: equal iterations, crossing tile boundaries.

questions.prompt: Why does Stream-K need a fix-up step?
options: Tiles covered by more than one block have several partial accumulators that must be summed
questions.explanation: Split tiles are finished by combining partials.

questions.prompt: 30 tiles, 16 SMs, 8 iterations per tile. Data-parallel time ÷ Stream-K time?
Why does the paper prefer a hybrid (data-parallel full waves + Stream-K remainder)?
options: Fewer split tiles: less fix-up traffic and better cache locality, with the same tail removal
questions.explanation: Split only what the tail needs.

questions.prompt: How many blocks does a Stream-K kernel launch?
options: About as many as the GPU can run at once (persistent blocks)
questions.explanation: Persistent blocks each loop over their share of iterations.
